00-Getting-Started.pdf.title: Getting Started
00-Getting-Started.pdf.subtitle: Signing in, the access key, getting around, settings and updates
00-Getting-Started.pdf.purpose: How to open the app at the start of a shift, sign in, find your way around, and keep the app up to date. Every other guide assumes you've done the steps here.
00-Getting-Started.pdf.need: The app link (ask a lead), and the store's access key the first time you use a new device.

steps.title: Install it on the store phone
body: Open the app link in Safari (not Chrome). Tap the Share icon, then Add to Home Screen → Add.
From then on, always open it from the home-screen icon. It runs full-screen and keeps working when the Wi-Fi drops.
steps.tip: The new app has its own icon, separate from the original one. Both can be installed while the store switches over.

steps.title: Enter the access key (first time only)
body: The first time a device opens the app, the sign-in screen shows an Access key box. Paste the store's key into it.
The app checks the key with the Google Sheet before saving it. “That key was rejected” means it was mistyped, or the key has changed: check with a lead.
Once it's saved you'll see “Access key saved on this device”, or “Using the access key from the original app” if that browser already had it.
steps.tip: An iPhone home-screen icon keeps its own storage, separate from Safari, so you may need to enter the key once on the icon even if Safari already has it.

steps.title: Pick your initials and tap Continue
body: Choose your initials from the list. Everything you do this shift is stamped with them, and the date is always added automatically.
Not on the list? Tap + Add new initials, type them, and tap Add. They're added to the shared roster for every device.
steps.tip: The app asks who's working every time it's opened, so a shared phone never keeps the last person's initials.

steps.title: Let it pull the latest from the sheet
body: After sign-in the app pulls the catalog, counts, consolidations, receiving and floor lists from the Google Sheet. This can take up to about 10 seconds.

If it's slow (weak signal), a Continue with what's saved on this device button appears after a few seconds. Tap it to start working: the pull carries on in the background and the screen updates when it's done.

steps.title: Get around with the bottom bar
body: Six pages: Home, Catalog, Counts, Consol (Consolidations), Receiving and Floor (Floor Stock). Each one has its own guide.
The red number on Home is how many things need someone's attention right now.

steps.title: The top bar
body: Initials: see who's signed in, or switch user. ↻ Refresh: pull the newest data from the sheet (use it after a lead pastes a new list into the sheet). ⚙ Settings: access key, staff roster, feedback and version.
An Offline badge appears next to the title when the device has no connection.

steps.title: Hand the phone to someone else
body: Tap your initials in the top bar, pick the new person's initials and tap Switch. Nothing else changes. Anything already staged stays where it is.

steps.title: Settings
body: The Google Sheet URL and Access key rarely need touching. If the key is ever changed, paste the new one here and tap Save & sync.
Staff roster shows everyone's initials, and you can add new ones here. The bottom line shows the app version and when it last synced.

steps.title: Leave feedback
body: Something broken, confusing or missing? In Settings tap Leave feedback, type it and tap Send. It goes straight to the Feedback tab of the sheet, tagged as coming from the new app.

steps.title: Install updates
body: When a new version is published, a bar appears at the top: “A new version is ready.” Tap Reload. That's all.

rows: “Couldn't reach the sheet — showing what's saved on this device.”
No connection, or Google was slow to answer.
Keep working; things you stage are kept on the device. Tap ↻ once you're back on Wi-Fi.
“The sheet rejected this device's access key.”
The key on this device is wrong or out of date.
⚙ Settings → paste the current key → Save & sync. Ask a lead for the key.
Stuck on the loading screen
The sheet is slow to answer.
Wait for Continue with what's saved on this device and tap it.
The app looks out of date
An older version is still loaded.
Close and reopen the app, then tap Reload on the update bar.

01-Home.pdf.title: Home
01-Home.pdf.subtitle: What needs attention right now, shortcuts, and this week's numbers
01-Home.pdf.purpose: Home is the first screen after sign-in. It answers one question: what needs someone's attention right now? It watches every other page and lists anything that's stuck, unsaved or waiting on MAO, so nobody has to tap through every page to find out.
01-Home.pdf.need: Signed in (see the Getting Started guide).

steps.title: Check how fresh the numbers are
body: Under the greeting, “Synced with the sheet” shows when the app last pulled everything from the Google Sheet.
If it's old, or a lead has just pasted something new into the sheet, tap ↻ in the top bar.

steps.title: Use a shortcut
body: Scan to Count opens Counts with the camera ready. Scan Packing Slip opens Consolidations ready to close a box. Scan Boxes opens Receiving in continuous box-scanning mode.

steps.title: Work through “Needs attention”
body: Each card is one thing that needs doing, with a button that takes you straight to the right page.

Red means act now, amber means soon, and grey cards are just notes (e.g. something staged on this device but not sent yet). A card disappears by itself once the problem is fixed. There's nothing to dismiss.
When there's nothing left you'll see “All clear.”

steps.title: Glance at this week's numbers
body: Count accuracy: the share of this week's counts that were within tolerance. Open consolidation lines: items on HQ's list not yet processed. Boxes received: boxes physically received this week. 86 Board: items currently out of stock.
Tap any tile to open that page. The week starts on Monday.

steps.title: Watch the badge
body: The red number on the Home button in the bottom bar is how many red and amber cards are waiting, so you can see it from any page. Grey notes aren't counted.

extras.text: What can appear on Home, and how to clear it

rows: Box on the shelf but not received into MAO
A box was marked Physically Received over a day ago, but not Received into MAO.
Receive it in MAO, then mark it Received into MAO on the Receiving page.
Count outside tolerance
The latest count of a product (last 14 days) was off by more than 2 units or 5%, whichever is larger.
Recount it on Counts. A recount within tolerance clears it.
Counts not saved to the sheet
Counts logged on this device haven't been sent yet.
Counts → Save to Sheet.
Consolidation items waiting in Holding
Items were marked Actioned but Update wasn't tapped. Turns amber after a day.
Consolidations → Update Sheet.
Consolidation adjustment unresolved
An old “Needs Adjustment” entry from the original app.
Consolidations → Activity → Resolve.
Floor item Needed for 3+ days
A size has sat on the Replen list for 3 or more days.
Floor Stock → Replen → Picked or Out of stock.
Staged in Receiving / Check Floor / Replen
Decisions held on this device only.
Tap the update button on that page.
The sheet rejected this device's access key
The key is wrong or has changed.
⚙ Settings → paste the current key.
Data may be out of date
No full sync in the last 24 hours.
Tap ↻ when connected.

02-Product-Catalog.pdf.title: Product Catalog
02-Product-Catalog.pdf.subtitle: Look up products, set hard-tag placement, and add new products from MAO
02-Product-Catalog.pdf.purpose: One place for everything about a product: its details, where its hard tag goes, and how it's been counted recently. It replaces the original app's Tag Lookup and Product Master tabs. New products are added here by pasting from MAO.
02-Product-Catalog.pdf.need: Signed in. To set a tag or import products you need a connection.

steps.title: Open the Catalog
body: Tap Catalog in the bottom bar. The line under the title shows how many products and styles are in the shared catalog.

steps.title: Search or scan for a product
body: Type any part of a SKU, UPC, style number or name. Results update as you type.
Or tap the camera button and scan the barcode. An exact barcode match opens that product straight away. Tap ✕ to clear.
steps.tip: Nothing found? The product isn't in the catalog yet. Add it with “Import from MAO” (step 6).

steps.title: Open a product's details
body: Tap Details on a result to see its style, color, size, dept, the expected count last used on this device, its hard-tag placement, and its most recent counts.
Count this product takes you to Counts with this product already loaded. Tap ‹ Back to results to return.

steps.title: Set or change the hard-tag placement
body: In the Hard-tag placement box, choose a location from the list (Hood, Below Wash Tag, Through Wash Tag, Tag Side Pocket, Left Leg In-seam, Chest Pocket, or No Hard Tag) and tap Save.
A tag location belongs to the whole style, so it's applied to every color and size of that style at once. The line under the box says how many variants that covers.
steps.tip: Use “No Hard Tag” for a style that genuinely doesn't get one, so nobody wonders whether it was just never set.

steps.title: Paste new products from MAO
body: Open Import from MAO. In MAO's View Inventory page, select and copy the product blocks, then paste them into the box.
Tap Import / Update. Products are matched by SKU: new ones are added, existing ones are refreshed. Expected counts are never overwritten.

steps.title: Check they reached the sheet
body: The message under the buttons confirms how many were added and that they were shared with the sheet, so every device now has them.
If it says only some were shared, check your connection and import the same paste again. Re-importing is safe.
steps.tip: Export CSV downloads the whole catalog as a spreadsheet file.

steps.title: Review every tag assignment
body: Open Hard-tag assignments to see every style that has a tag location set. Tap one to open that product and change it.

03-Counts.pdf.title: Counts
03-Counts.pdf.subtitle: Scan, count, and save inventory counts to the shared log
03-Counts.pdf.purpose: Cycle counting. Scan or find a product, confirm the expected quantity, enter what's actually there, and the difference is logged. Counts that are off by too much are flagged so they get a second look instead of disappearing into a list.
03-Counts.pdf.need: Signed in. Counting works offline, and you send the counts to the sheet when you're connected.

steps.title: Start a count
body: Tap Scan Product to Count and scan the product's barcode. If you can't scan, type in the search box underneath (step 2).

steps.title: Or search for it
body: Type any part of the SKU, UPC, style or name and tap Count on the right result.

steps.title: Enter expected and actual
body: The card shows the product and when it was last counted, and by whom.
Expected is pre-filled with the last expected count used on this device. Confirm or correct it. Type what you actually counted into Actual, then tap Log Count (or press Enter).

steps.title: Read the result
body: The message tells you whether the count matched, or was over or under and by how much.
If it's off by more than 2 units or 5% (whichever is larger), it's flagged as outside tolerance. It shows in red here and as a card on Home until it's recounted.

steps.title: Scanned something that isn't in the catalog?
body: A Not in the catalog yet form opens with the barcode filled in. Enter at least the SKU and Description (style, dept, color and size if you have them) and tap Add Product.
It's added to the shared catalog and loaded straight into the count.

steps.title: Save to Sheet
body: Counts are kept on this device until you tap Save to Sheet. The button shows how many are waiting, and unsent counts carry a not saved tag.
Saving sends every unsent count in one go. If the connection fails, nothing is lost: they stay queued, so just tap Save again later.
steps.tip: Save before you hand the device to someone else and at the end of your shift. Home reminds you if anything is left unsaved.

steps.title: Recount anything outside tolerance
body: Tap the Outside tolerance filter to see only flagged counts, then tap Recount to load that product again.
The flag clears once the newest count of that product is within tolerance. Not saved shows only unsent counts, and All shows everything. CSV downloads the full log.

04-Consolidations.pdf.title: Consolidations
04-Consolidations.pdf.subtitle: Pull HQ's consolidation list, track counts, and log closed boxes
04-Consolidations.pdf.purpose: Working through HQ's consolidation list: tracking how many of each item you've pulled, marking lines done, and recording who closed each box and when.
04-Consolidations.pdf.need: A lead pastes HQ's list into the ConsolMaster tab of the Google Sheet. Tap ↻ in the top bar to load a new list. The full process is in the Consolidations Guide linked at the top of the page.

steps.title: Find the items to consolidate
body: Each line is one item on HQ's list: name, color, style and destination, with your pulled count against the total HQ wants.
Use the filter box above the list to narrow it by name, style, color or destination.

steps.title: Track what you've pulled
body: Tap + / − as you pull pieces, or type the number. Each change saves to the sheet immediately, so everyone sees the same running count.
The line turns green once you've reached the total.

steps.title: Mark a line Actioned
body: When a line is done, tap Actioned. It moves out of the list into Holding, where it waits until you tap Update Sheet.
Changed your mind? Tap Remove in Holding to put it back.

steps.title: Update the sheet
body: Tap Update Sheet to send everything in Holding at once. Each line is marked Processed on HQ's list and logged in Activity with your initials.
If it can't reach the sheet, the items stay in Holding. Try again when you're connected.
steps.tip: Lines left in Holding show up on Home, and turn amber after a day, so nothing gets forgotten.

steps.title: Close a box
body: When a box is sealed, tap Scan Packing Slip and scan the slip's barcode. If it won't scan, type the reference number and tap Close Box.
This only records the reference number, who closed it and when. The box's contents are looked up in MAO by that number.

steps.title: Confirm it's closed in MAO
body: A reminder appears every time: this app can't see MAO. Close the box in MAO first, then tap It's closed in MAO, log it.

steps.title: Check it was logged
body: A green message confirms the box was closed and logged. It also appears at the top of Activity. CSV downloads the full consolidation log.

05-Receiving.pdf.title: Receiving
05-Receiving.pdf.subtitle: Import shipments, scan boxes in, and make sure MAO gets updated
05-Receiving.pdf.purpose: Logging incoming boxes in two separate steps: Physically Received (it's on our shelf) and Received into MAO (MAO knows about it). Each step is stamped with who did it and when. Boxes that are on the shelf but not yet in MAO stay visible until they are. Then leadership double check in MAO that each box really was received there.
05-Receiving.pdf.need: The expected-shipment list from MAO's Receive Inventory page (step 1).

steps.title: Import the expected shipments
body: Open Import from MAO at the top of the page. In MAO's Receive Inventory page, copy the shipment list (the ETA / Package / PO # blocks) and paste it in.
Tap Import. The boxes appear under Expected boxes and are shared with every device. Re-importing the same list is safe.

steps.title: Scan boxes as they come in
body: Tap Scan Boxes. The camera stays open, so scan each box's package barcode one after another. Each one goes into Holding and the count updates on screen.
Tap Done Scanning when you're finished.

steps.title: A box that isn't on the list
body: If a scanned box wasn't in the import, the camera stops and asks for its PO #. Enter it and tap Add & hold. The box is added to the shared list and held, ready to mark.

steps.title: Mark them Physically Received
body: With the boxes in Holding, tap Physically Received. They're stamped with today's date and your initials.
Tap Remove to take a box back out of Holding before marking.

steps.title: Watch “Waiting on MAO”
body: Boxes that are on the shelf but not yet received into MAO are listed here, each showing how long it has been waiting.
After a day, a box also shows up as a red card on Home. This is the step that's easy to forget, and it's what this list is for.

steps.title: Receive them into MAO
body: Receive the boxes in MAO first, and press Submit in MAO on the store phone. Then tap Hold all on Waiting on MAO (or scan just the boxes you did) and tap Received into MAO.

steps.title: Confirm you pressed Submit
body: An orange check asks Did you press Submit in MAO? Boxes don't count as received in MAO until Submit is pressed on the store phone, so look in MAO and make sure each box shows as received.
Tap I pressed Submit and checked MAO to mark them. The boxes drop off every list and the Home card clears. Go back leaves them in Holding.
steps.tip: Boxes marked here but never submitted in MAO cause inventory errors. That's why every one is double checked by leadership afterwards.

steps.title: No camera? Tick boxes instead
body: Under Expected boxes, tick the boxes and tap Hold selected. Then mark them as in steps 4 and 6. Use the filter to find a PO # or package number quickly.
Export CSV (inside Import from MAO) downloads the full receiving log.

steps.title: Leadership: Double Check Required
body: Leadership (SG, SC, OT, JB, AL, MS) see an orange Double Check Required button on Home whenever boxes marked Received into MAO in the last 14 days haven't been checked yet. Tap it to open the Double Check tab in Receiving.

steps.title: Leadership: check each box in MAO
body: Look up each package in MAO and confirm it was received and submitted. Then tap Checked. It saves straight away, with no Holding step, and the box drops off the list.

Each check is stamped in the sheet's ReceivingLog tab under DOUBLE CHECKED (when) and DOUBLE CHECKED BY (your initials). If a box isn't received in MAO, receive and submit it there first, then check it.

06-Floor-Stock.pdf.title: Floor Stock
06-Floor-Stock.pdf.subtitle: Check the floor after sales, pick replen, and run the 86 Board
06-Floor-Stock.pdf.purpose: Keeping the floor stocked after things sell, in three tabs that follow one item from start to finish: Check Floor (what sold, and is it needed?) → Replen (pick it from the back) → 86 Board (we're out, and that's been noted).
06-Floor-Stock.pdf.need: A lead pastes MAO's Items Sold export (columns A–H) into the FloorRestock tab of the sheet. Tap ↻ to load it. Accessories (gender “U”) are left out automatically, since they're restocked from the floor.

steps.title: Open Check Floor
body: Tap Floor in the bottom bar, then the Check Floor tab. The numbers on the tabs show how much is waiting in each.
The line under the title shows when the floor was last checked, and by whom.

steps.title: One line per style and color
body: Sold items are grouped into one line per style + color, whatever size sold. For example, Black Atom Hoodies sold in S, M and L show as one Atom Hoody Men's · Black · 4 sold line.
Go to that style on the floor and see for yourself which sizes are missing.

steps.title: Needed? Pick the sizes
body: If the floor needs restocking, tap Needed and pick the sizes that are missing, or Other (any size) if any size will do. Then tap Stage as Needed.
If the floor is fine, tap Not needed.
steps.tip: Only the sizes you pick go to Replen. The sizes that sold don't matter. What matters is what you saw missing.

steps.title: Update the sheet
body: Your decisions wait in Holding (tap Remove to undo one). Tap Update Sheet to send them all.
The sizes you picked appear on the Replen tab for whoever is picking in the back.

steps.title: Something needs restocking but isn't on the list
body: Type it into “Something not on the list?” at the top. If it's in the catalog, tap Add on the result and it joins the Check Floor list.
Not in the catalog at all? Tap Not in the catalog? Add “…” by hand, pick the sizes and tap Add as Needed. It's staged as Needed, ready for Update.

steps.title: Pick on the Replen tab
body: Replen lists each style and color once, with the needed sizes underneath. For each size, tap Picked once it's on the floor, or Out of stock if there's none in the back.
An amber needed … days note means it has been waiting 3 or more days. It's also flagged on Home.

steps.title: Update Replen
body: Picks wait in Holding until you tap Update Sheet. Anything marked Out of stock goes onto the 86 Board.

steps.title: Run the 86 Board
body: The 86 Board lists everything that's out, newest first, so the floor team can see it without calling the back.
When stock comes back, tap Restocked. It saves straight away and the item drops off the board.

extras.text: Lines on Replen and the 86 Board carry a small three-step bar: Needed → Picked / Out of stock → Restocked. A red middle segment means the item went out of stock. A green label means it's finished.
